question: A food delivery person can either have shifts on bikes or scooters. A shift on a bike can deliver 10 orders, takes 5 units of energy, and brings in $50 on tips because it is faster. A shift on a scooter can deliver 7 orders, takes 6 units of energy, and brings in $43 on tips.  The delivery person has available 40 shifts a month and has 230 units of energy and must bring at least 320 orders. He must have at least 5 shifts on a scooter because bikes are harder to get. How many shifts on each type of transportation should the delivery person schedule to maximize tips received?

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # shift types
    "shifts": ["bike", "scooter"],
    # per-type shift data
    "orders":   {"bike": 10, "scooter": 7},
    "energy":   {"bike": 5,  "scooter": 6},
    "tips":     {"bike": 50, "scooter": 43},
    # limits / requirements
    "shift_budget":  40,   # at most 40 shifts a month
    "energy_budget": 230,  # at most 230 units of energy
    "min_orders":    320,  # at least 320 orders
    "min_scooter":   5,    # at least 5 scooter shifts
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data if data is not None else DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="delivery_shift_scheduling")

    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=d["shifts"])  # shift types

    # x[s]: number of shifts (nonneg integer)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.S, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # objective: maximize tips received
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(d["tips"][s] * model.x[s] for s in model.S),
        sense=pyo.maximize,
    )

    # source sentence: "The delivery person has available 40 shifts a month."
    def available_shifts_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.S) <= d["shift_budget"]
    model.available_shifts = pyo.Constraint(rule=available_shifts_rule)

    # source sentence: "has 230 units of energy."
    def energy_rule(m):
        return sum(d["energy"][s] * m.x[s] for s in m.S) <= d["energy_budget"]
    model.energy_limit = pyo.Constraint(rule=energy_rule)

    # source sentence: "must bring at least 320 orders."
    def orders_rule(m):
        return sum(d["orders"][s] * m.x[s] for s in m.S) >= d["min_orders"]
    model.orders_required = pyo.Constraint(rule=orders_rule)

    # source sentence: "must have at least 5 shifts on a scooter"
    def scooter_rule(m):
        return m.x["scooter"] >= d["min_scooter"]
    model.scooter_min = pyo.Constraint(rule=scooter_rule)

    return model

        return sum(d["orders"][i] * m.x[i] for i in m.I) >= d["orders_required"]

    model.c3 = pyo.Constraint(rule=c3_rule)

    def c4_rule(m):
        return m.x["scooter"] >= d["scooter_min"]

    model.c4 = pyo.Constraint(rule=c4_rule)

    return model
